title: Review: opinions
why: Review of unit 11: you bring together everything you need for a real discussion in Hebrew: giving your opinion, backing it up with שֶׁ clauses, imagining with the conditional and understanding a news story in the passive. It's the last step before the everyday Hebrew of unit 12.

In a debate, a good answer often has three steps: your opinion, your reason, then a concession.

לְדַעְתִּי, לַעֲבֹד מֵהַבַּיִת זֶה נוֹחַ, כִּי אֵין פְּקָקִים. מִצַּד שֵׁנִי, בַּבַּיִת אֲנִי קְצָת בּוֹדֵד.In my opinion, working from home is convenient, because there are no traffic jams. On the other hand, at home I'm a bit lonely. [leda'ati, la'avod me-ha-bayit ze no'akh, ki ein pkakim. mi-tsad sheni, ba-bayit ani ktsat boded]

Just like in casual English (\"working from home, it's so convenient\"), spoken Hebrew picks the idea up again with זֶה: לַעֲבֹד מֵהַבַּיִת זֶה נוֹחַ.

Unit reminders

  • שֶׁ links everything: הֶעָמִית שֶׁגָּר רָחוֹק (the coworker who lives far away), כְּשֶׁאֲנִי בַּמִּשְׂרָד (when I'm at the office).
  • The conditional: הָיִיתִי + present. לוּ גַּרְתִּי קָרוֹב, הָיִיתִי בָּא בָּרֶגֶל (if I lived nearby, I would walk here).
  • The passive: נִ at the start for the nif'al, the u sound for the pu'al and the huf'al: הַמִּשְׂרָד שֻׁפַּץ (the office was renovated), הֻחְלַט שֶׁ… (it was decided that…).
הֻחְלַט שֶׁכֻּלָּם עוֹבְדִים מֵהַבַּיִת שְׁנֵי יָמִים בְּשָׁבוּעַ.It was decided that everyone works from home two days a week. [hukhlat she-kulam ovdim me-ha-bayit shnei yamim be-shavua]

The two traps of the unit: כְּשֶׁ (when, in a statement) is not מָתַי? (when, in a question); and כִּי goes before a clause, בִּגְלַל before a noun.
